title: حِكَايَةُ قَمَرِ الزَّمَانِ
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 2, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 27–28 (Night 233, continuing nights-232), transcribed from the scan (archive.org aliflailaorbook02unkngoog) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm as Macnaghten prints it, except where a clear misprint has been corrected (each is noted). Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition’s Middle Arabic forms, is preserved; clear misprints are corrected in the text, and the note on each gives the print’s reading. Obscure or doubtful forms are kept as printed, vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 233 continues the tale of Qamar al-Zamān. Bahādur, condemned for the dead woman, takes the blame on himself, and the king orders him hanged; the crier parades him through the streets. Hearing it, al-Amjad will not let the man who sheltered him die for his deed: he goes to the governor, confesses that he killed her, and before the king tells his whole story and his brother's. The king pardons him, makes him his vizier, rewards Bahādur, and has the crier search the city for al-Asʿad, in vain. Meanwhile al-Asʿad has been tormented by the Magians for a whole year, and as their feast draws near Bahrām the Magian makes ready a ship; and morning overtakes Shahrazād. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ الثَّالِثَةُ وَالثَّلٰثُونَ بَعْدَ الْمِائَتَيْنِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-thālithatu wa-al-thalāthūna baʿda al-miʾatayni
sentences.l: And when it was the night, the third and the thirty after the two-hundred,
sentences.i: And when it was the two hundred and thirty-third night,
sentences.n: The night's opening formula: the unit, al-thālithatu, comes before the tens and is joined to them by wa-, all in the nominative with al-laylatu. thalāthūn is printed without its middle alif, والثلٰثون, with the dagger alif already set; the ئ of المائتين is printed.

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُ أَنَّ بَهَادُرَ أَطْرَقَ بِرَأْسِهِ إِلَى الْأَرْضِ قُدَّامَ الْمَلِكِ
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu anna Bahādura aṭraqa bi-raʾsihi ilā al-arḍi quddāma al-maliki
sentences.l: She-said: It-has-reached-me, O fortunate king, that Bahādur bowed with-his-head to the-ground before the-king.
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that Bahādur hung his head to the ground before the king.
sentences.n: The print has اطراق, a misprint for اطرق, corrected here: aṭraqa, Form IV, 'to bow the head and keep silent', the verb on which the night before broke off. There it took raʾsahu as a direct object; here the print has bi-raʾsihi, 'with his head', bi- marking the part bowed, as the verb allows either way. The hamza of برأسه is printed. Bahādura is a diptote, the noun of anna, so -a without tanwīn.

sentences.t: فَصَرَخَ الْمَلِكُ عَلَيْهِ وَقَالَ لَهُ وَيْلَكَ مَنْ قَتَلَ هٰذِهِ الصَّبِيَّةَ
sentences.tr: fa-ṣarakha al-maliku ʿalayhi wa-qāla lahu waylaka man qatala hādhihi al-ṣabiyyata
sentences.l: And-shouted the-king at-him and-said to-him: Woe-to-you! Who killed this the-girl?
sentences.i: The king shouted at him, “Woe to you! Who killed this girl?”
sentences.n: ṣarakha ʿalā, 'to shout at': ʿalā marks the one shouted at. The fatḥa of مَن is printed, to show it is man, 'who?', and not min, 'from'. hādhihi takes a dagger alif.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ يَا سَيِّدِي أَنَا قَتَلْتُهَا وَلَاحَوْلَ وَلَاقُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللّٰهِ الْعَلِيِّ الْعَظِيمِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu yā sayyidī anā qataltuhā wa-lā ḥawla wa-lā quwwata illā bi-allāhi al-ʿaliyyi al-ʿaẓīmi
sentences.l: And-he-said to-him: O my-lord, I killed-her; and-no power and-no strength except in-God, the-High, the-Mighty.
sentences.i: “My lord,” he said to him, “I killed her; and there is no power and no strength save in God, the High, the Mighty.”
sentences.n: Bahādur takes the blame to shield al-Amjad. lā ḥawla wa-lā quwwata illā bi-allāhi, 'there is no power and no strength except through God', the formula of resignation (the ḥawqala): lā denies the whole kind, so ḥawla and quwwata are accusative without tanwīn, and bi- is 'through, by means of'. The print runs both ولاحول and ولاقوة together; kept as set. The shaddas of الّا and العليّ are printed.

sentences.t: فَغَضِبَ الْمَلِكُ وَأَمَرَ بِشَنْقِهِ فَنَزَلَ بِهِ السَّيَّافُ حِينَ أَمَرَهُ الْمَلِكُ
sentences.tr: fa-ghaḍiba al-maliku wa-amara bi-shanqihi fa-nazala bihi al-sayyāfu ḥīna amarahu al-maliku
sentences.l: And-was-angry the-king and-ordered (the) hanging-(of)-him; and-came-down with-him the-swordsman when ordered-him the-king.
sentences.i: The king was enraged and ordered him to be hanged, and the executioner took him down the moment the king gave the order.
sentences.n: The print has امرة, a misprint for امره, corrected here: amarahu, 'he ordered him'. amara bi-, 'to order (something)': the verb takes bi- for the thing ordered, bi-shanqihi, 'his hanging'; shanq is the verbal noun of shanaqa, 'to hang', with its object as the suffix. nazala bihi, 'came down with him': bi- marks the one taken along, down from the palace to the town. al-sayyāf, 'the swordsman', is the executioner, whatever his means; its shadda is printed.

sentences.t: وَنَزَلَ الْوَالِي بِالْمُنَادِي يُنَادِي فِي أَزِقَّةِ الْمَدِينَةِ بِالْفُرْجَةِ عَلَي بَهَادُرَ أَمِيرِ يَا خُورِ الْمَلِكِ وَدَارَ بِهِ فِى الْأَزِقَّةِ وَالْأَسْوَاقِ
sentences.tr: wa-nazala al-wālī bi-al-munādī yunādī fī aziqqati al-madīnati bi-al-furjati ʿalā Bahādura amīri yākhūri al-maliki wa-dāra bihi fī al-aziqqati wa-al-aswāqi
sentences.l: And-came-down the-governor with-the-crier crying in (the) lanes (of) the-city with-the-spectacle upon Bahādur, (the) commander (of the) stable (of) the-king, and-he-went-round with-him in the-lanes and-the-markets.
sentences.i: The chief of police came down with the crier, who cried through the lanes of the city that all should come and see the show made of Bahādur, the king's master of the horse; and he paraded him through the lanes and the markets.
sentences.n: nazala bi-, 'to come down with': bi- marks the crier he brings along. yunādī, 'crying', describes what the crier did as he went. nādā bi-, 'to cry out (news of)': bi- marks what is proclaimed, al-furja, 'the spectacle', and ʿalā marks the one made a spectacle of: the crier calls the town to come and look at Bahādur being led to his death. علي is the print's spelling of ʿalā, with ي; kept as set. amīr yākhūr, 'master of the horse', vocalised as in the night before; here the print sets يا خور as two words, where it has been one, ياخور; kept as set, and read as the one title, amīri yākhūri al-maliki, in apposition to Bahādura and so genitive. dāra bihi, 'he went round with him': bi- marks the one paraded. The shadda of الازقّة is printed, not that of ازقة before it. فى is printed with ى; kept as set.

sentences.t: هٰذَا مَا كَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِ بَهَادُرَ
sentences.tr: hādhā mā kāna min amri Bahādura
sentences.l: This (is) what was of (the) affair (of) Bahādur.
sentences.i: So much for Bahādur.
sentences.n: The storyteller's formula for leaving one thread of the tale to take up another. Bahādura is genitive, a diptote, so -a. hādhā takes a dagger alif.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا مَا كَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِ الْأَمْجَدِ فَإِنَّهُ لَمَّا طَلَعَ عَلَيْهِ النَّهَارُ وَارْتَفَعَتِ الشَّمْسُ وَلَمْ يَعُدْ إِلَيْهِ بَهَادُرُ قَالَ لَاحَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللّٰهِ الْعَلِيِّ الْعَظِيمِ
sentences.tr: wa-ammā mā kāna min amri al-Amjadi fa-innahu lammā ṭalaʿa ʿalayhi al-nahāru wa-irtafaʿati al-shamsu wa-lam yaʿud ilayhi Bahāduru qāla lā ḥawla wa-lā quwwata illā bi-allāhi al-ʿaliyyi al-ʿaẓīmi
sentences.l: And-as-for what was of (the) affair (of) al-Amjad, then-indeed-he, when rose upon-him the-day and-rose-high the-sun and-not returned to-him Bahādur, he-said: No power and-no strength except in-God, the-High, the-Mighty.
sentences.i: As for al-Amjad: when day broke upon him and the sun climbed high, and Bahādur had not come back to him, he said, “There is no power and no strength save in God, the High, the Mighty!”
sentences.n: ammā … fa-, 'as for …, (then)': fa- opens what is said about the topic. ṭalaʿa ʿalayhi al-nahāru, 'the day rose upon him': ʿalā marks the one it finds there. lam yaʿud, jussive of ʿāda, 'he did not return'. This time the print sets لاحول as one word but ولا قوة as two; kept as set. The shaddas of الّا and العليّ are printed.

sentences.t: يَا تُرَى أَيُّ شَيْءٍ تَمَّ عَلَيْهِ وَمَاجَرَى لَهُ
sentences.tr: yā turā ayyu shayʾin tamma ʿalayhi wa-mā jarā lahu
sentences.l: O is-it-seen, what thing came-to-pass upon-him, and-what befell to-him?
sentences.i: “I wonder what has happened to him, and what has befallen him?”
sentences.n: yā turā, 'O, is it to be seen?', is the later Arabic 'I wonder': turā is the passive of yarā, 'it is seen'. tamma ʿalā, 'to come to pass upon, befall': ʿalā marks the one it falls on. mā jarā lahu, 'what ran to him', what befell him: li- here marks the one it happened to; printed run together, وماجرى, kept as set. The shaddas of ايّ and تمّ and the ء of شيء are printed.

sentences.t: فَبَيْنَمَا هُوَ يَتَفَكَّرُ وَإِذَا بِالْمُنَادِي يُنَادِي بِالْفُرْجَةِ عَلَى بَهَادُرَ فَإِنَّهُمْ يَشْنُقُونَهُ فِي وَسَطِ النَّهَارِ
sentences.tr: fa-baynamā huwa yatafakkaru wa-idhā bi-al-munādī yunādī bi-al-furjati ʿalā Bahādura fa-innahum yashnuqūnahu fī wasaṭi al-nahāri
sentences.l: And-while he (was) pondering, and-behold the-crier crying with-the-spectacle upon Bahādur, for-indeed-they (are) hanging-him in (the) middle (of) the-day.
sentences.i: While he was turning this over in his mind, there was the crier, calling on all to come and see the show made of Bahādur, for they were hanging him at midday.
sentences.n: baynamā …, wa-idhā bi-, 'while …, behold': the bi- after idhā of surprise only marks what appears, the crier. As before, nādā bi- marks what is proclaimed and ʿalā the one made a spectacle of. fa-innahum yashnuqūnahu, 'for they are hanging him': the imperfect is the crier's and the town's present, 'they are about to hang him'. wasaṭ al-nahār, 'the middle of the day', noon. The shadda of يتفكّر is printed.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ الْأَمْجَدُ ذٰلِكَ بَكَى وَقَالَ إِنَّا لِلّٰهِ وَإِنَّا إِلَيْهِ رَاجِعُونَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-Amjadu dhālika bakā wa-qāla innā li-allāhi wa-innā ilayhi rājiʿūna
sentences.l: And-when heard al-Amjad that, he-wept and-said: Indeed-we (are) for-God, and-indeed-we to-Him (are) returning.
sentences.i: When al-Amjad heard this he wept and said, “We belong to God, and to Him we return.”
sentences.n: innā li-allāhi wa-innā ilayhi rājiʿūna, the Qurʾānic formula (2:156) spoken at news of death or disaster: li- here is of belonging, 'we are God's'. The shaddas of انّا and للّه are printed. dhālika takes a dagger alif.

sentences.t: قَدْ أَرَادَ هَلَاكَ نَفْسِهِ ظُلْمًا مِنْ أَجْلِي وَأَنَا الَّذِي قَتَلْتُهَا
sentences.tr: qad arāda halāka nafsihi ẓulman min ajlī wa-anā alladhī qataltuhā
sentences.l: He-has wanted (the) destruction (of) his-self wrongfully for (the) sake (of) me, and-I (am the) one-who killed-her.
sentences.i: “He has chosen to go to his death unjustly for my sake, when it was I who killed her.”
sentences.n: halāka nafsihi, 'the destruction of himself'. ẓulman, 'wrongfully', an adverbial accusative: he dies though innocent. min ajlī, 'for my sake'. wa-anā alladhī qataltuhā is circumstantial, 'when I am the one who killed her'; after alladhī the verb is first person, agreeing with anā.

sentences.t: وَاللّٰهِ لَا كَانَ هٰذَا أَبَدًا
sentences.tr: wa-allāhi lā kāna hādhā abadan
sentences.l: By-God, may-not-be this ever!
sentences.i: “By God, that shall never be!”
sentences.n: lā with the perfect in a wish, 'may it not be', as in the night before; there the print set لاكان as one word, here as two, لا كان; kept as set. hādhā takes a dagger alif.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ خَرَجَ مِنَ الْقَاعَةِ وَقَفَلَهَا وَشَقَّ فِي وَسَطِ الْمَدِينَةِ حَتَّى أَتَى إِلَى بَهَادُرَ
sentences.tr: thumma kharaja mina al-qāʿati wa-qafalahā wa-shaqqa fī wasaṭi al-madīnati ḥattā atā ilā Bahādura
sentences.l: Then he-went-out from the-hall and-locked-it and-cut in (the) middle (of) the-city until he-came to Bahādur.
sentences.i: Then he left the hall, locked it, and made his way through the heart of the city until he reached Bahādur.
sentences.n: qafala, 'to lock'. shaqqa fī, 'to make one's way through': fī marks what is crossed. atā ilā, 'he came to'. The shadda of شقّ is printed.

sentences.t: وَوَقَفَ قُدَّامَ الْوَالِي وَقَالَ لَهُ يَاسَيِّدِي لَاتَقْتُلْ بَهَادُرَ فَإِنَّهُ بَرِيءٌ وَاللّٰهِ مَا قَتَلَهَا إِلَّا أَنَا
sentences.tr: wa-waqafa quddāma al-wālī wa-qāla lahu yā sayyidī lā taqtul Bahādura fa-innahu barīʾun wa-allāhi mā qatalahā illā anā
sentences.l: And-he-stood before the-governor and-said to-him: O-my-lord, do-not kill Bahādur, for-indeed-he (is) innocent; by-God, not killed-her except I.
sentences.i: He stood before the chief of police and said to him, “My lord, do not kill Bahādur, for he is innocent. By God, none killed her but I.”
sentences.n: lā taqtul, prohibitive jussive, 'do not kill'; printed run together, لاتقتل, as is ياسيدي; both kept as set. mā … illā anā, 'none but I': the restriction puts the weight on anā. The ء of بريء and the shadda of الّا are printed.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ الْوَالِي كَلَامَهُ أَخَذَهُ هُوَ وَبَهَادُرُ وَطَلَعَ بِهِمَا إِلَى الْمَلِكِ وَأَعْلَمَهُ بِمَا سَمِعَهُ مِنَ الْأَمْجَدِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-wālī kalāmahu akhadhahu huwa wa-Bahāduru wa-ṭalaʿa bihimā ilā al-maliki wa-aʿlamahu bi-mā samiʿahu mina al-Amjadi
sentences.l: And-when heard the-governor his-speech, he-took-him, he and-Bahādur, and-went-up with-the-two to the-king, and-informed-him of-what he-had-heard-it from al-Amjad.
sentences.i: When the chief of police heard what he said, he took him and Bahādur both and brought them up to the king, and told him what he had heard from al-Amjad.
sentences.n: The print has اخذة, a misprint for اخذه, corrected here: akhadhahu, 'he took him'. huwa wa-Bahāduru, in the nominative, restates the -hu and adds Bahādur to it, the same loose Middle Arabic apposition as huwa wa-al-fardu in the night before. ṭalaʿa bi-, 'to go up with', so 'to bring up' to the palace: bi- marks those taken along. aʿlama bi-, 'to inform of': the verb takes bi- for the matter.

sentences.t: فَنَظَرَ الْمَلِكُ إِلَى الْأَمْجَدِ وَقَالَ لَهُ أَ أَنْتَ قَتَلْتَ الصَّبِيَّةَ
sentences.tr: fa-naẓara al-maliku ilā al-Amjadi wa-qāla lahu a-anta qatalta al-ṣabiyyata
sentences.l: And-looked the-king at al-Amjad and-said to-him: Is-it you (who) killed the-girl?
sentences.i: The king looked at al-Amjad and said to him, “Was it you who killed the girl?”
sentences.n: a- is the question particle; put before anta it asks about the person, 'was it you?'. The print sets it apart, أ أنت, with both hamzas printed; kept as set. The shadda of الصبيّة is printed.

sentences.t: قَالَ نَعَمْ
sentences.tr: qāla naʿam
sentences.l: He-said: Yes.
sentences.i: “Yes,” he said.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الْمَلِكُ احْكِ لِي مَا سَبَبُ قَتْلِكَ إِيَّاهَا وَاصْدُقْنِي
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-maliku iḥki lī mā sababu qatlika iyyāhā wa-uṣduqnī
sentences.l: And-said to-him the-king: Tell to-me what (is the) cause (of) your-killing her, and-tell-me-the-truth.
sentences.i: The king said to him, “Tell me why you killed her, and tell me the truth.”
sentences.n: iḥki, imperative of ḥakā, 'to tell, relate', its final long vowel dropped, leaving a short kasra; the kasra of احكِ is printed. li- marks the one told. qatlika iyyāhā, 'your killing her': the verbal noun takes its subject as the suffix -ka, so its object stands apart as iyyāhā. ṣadaqahu, 'to speak the truth to (someone)', takes the person as direct object: uṣduqnī, 'be truthful with me'. The shadda of ايّاها is printed.

sentences.t: قَالَ لَهُ أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ إِنَّهُ جَرَى لِي حَدِيثٌ عَجِيبٌ وَأَمْرٌ غَرِيبٌ لَوْكُتِبَ بِالْإِبَرِ عَلَى آمَاقِ الْبَصَرِ لَكَانَ عِبْرَةً لِمَنِ اعْتَبَرَ
sentences.tr: qāla lahu ayyuhā al-maliku innahu jarā lī ḥadīthun ʿajībun wa-amrun gharībun law kutiba bi-al-ibari ʿalā āmāqi al-baṣari la-kāna ʿibratan li-mani iʿtabara
sentences.l: He-said to-him: O king, indeed-it, there-ran to-me a-tale wondrous and-an-affair strange; if it-were-written with-the-needles on (the) inner-corners (of) the-eye, it-would-be a-lesson for-whoever takes-heed.
sentences.i: He said to him, “O king, a wondrous tale and a strange affair have befallen me. Were it written with needles on the inner corners of the eye, it would be a lesson to all who would take heed.”
sentences.n: A stock rhymed phrase of the Nights, rhyming ʿajīb / gharīb and then al-baṣar / iʿtabara. innahu, 'indeed it (is that)', the pronoun of the matter. jarā lī, 'befell me': li- marks the one it happened to. law kutiba … la-kāna, an unreal condition, 'if it were written …, it would be': the la- of la-kāna opens its answer. bi-al-ibari, 'with needles': bi- of the instrument; ibar is the plural of ibra. āmāq, plural of muʾq, the inner corner of the eye; the madda of آماق is printed: a tale so worth keeping that it should be pricked into the eye itself. li-man iʿtabara, 'for whoever takes warning': li- marks those it profits. The print runs law and kutiba together, لوكتب; kept as set.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ حَكَى لِلْمَلِكِ حَدِيثَهُ وَأَخْبَرَهُ بِمَا جَرَى لَهُ وَلِأَخِيهِ مِنَ الْمُبْتَدَأِ إِلَى الْمُنْتَهَى
sentences.tr: thumma ḥakā li-al-maliki ḥadīthahu wa-akhbarahu bi-mā jarā lahu wa-li-akhīhi mina al-mubtadaʾi ilā al-muntahā
sentences.l: Then he-told to-the-king his-story and-informed-him of-what befell to-him and-to-his-brother, from the-beginning to the-end.
sentences.i: Then he told the king his story, and all that had befallen him and his brother from first to last.
sentences.n: The print has واخبرة, a misprint for واخبره, corrected here: wa-akhbarahu, 'and he informed him'. li-al-maliki: li- marks the one told. akhbara bi-, 'to inform of': bi- marks the matter. jarā lahu wa-li-akhīhi: li- marks those it befell. al-mubtadaʾ and al-muntahā, 'the starting-point' and 'the end', passive participles of Form VIII used as nouns of place; the hamza of المبتدأ is printed.

sentences.t: فَتَعَجَّبَ الْمَلِكُ مِنْ ذٰلِكَ غَايَةَ الْعَجَبِ
sentences.tr: fa-taʿajjaba al-maliku min dhālika ghāyata al-ʿajabi
sentences.l: And-marvelled the-king from that (the) utmost (of) the-marvelling.
sentences.i: The king marvelled at it beyond measure.
sentences.n: taʿajjaba min, 'to wonder at': min marks the cause. ghāyata al-ʿajabi, 'the utmost of wonder', stands in for a cognate accusative and intensifies the verb. The shadda of تعجّب is printed.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ لَهُ اعْلَمْ أَنِّي قَدْ عَلِمْتُ أَنَّكَ مَعْذُورٌ وَلٰكِنْ يَا فَتَى هَلْ لَكَ أَنْ تَكُونَ عِنْدِي وَزِيرًا
sentences.tr: wa-qāla lahu iʿlam annī qad ʿalimtu annaka maʿdhūrun wa-lākin yā fatā hal laka an takūna ʿindī wazīran
sentences.l: And-he-said to-him: Know that-I have known that-you (are) excused; but, O young-man, is (it) for-you that you-be with-me a-vizier?
sentences.i: And he said to him, “Know that I see you were not to blame. But, young man, would you like to be my vizier?”
sentences.n: maʿdhūr, 'excused', one who has an excuse and is not to blame. hal laka an …, 'have you (a mind) to …?', the polite way to make an offer: li- marks the one whose wish is asked. ʿindī, 'with me', in my service. The damma of علمتُ is printed. lākin takes a dagger alif.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ سَمْعًا وَطَاعَةً
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu samʿan wa-ṭāʿatan
sentences.l: And-he-said to-him: Hearing and-obedience.
sentences.i: He answered him, with hearing and obedience.
sentences.n: samʿan wa-ṭāʿatan, accusatives standing for 'I hear and obey', the reply of one who accepts a command.

sentences.t: فَخَلَعَ عَلَيْهِ الْمَلِكُ وَعَلَى بَهَادُرَ خِلَعًا سَنِيَّةً وَأَعْطَاهُ دَارًا حَسَنَةً وَخَدَمًا وَحَشَمًا
sentences.tr: fa-khalaʿa ʿalayhi al-maliku wa-ʿalā Bahādura khilaʿan saniyyatan wa-aʿṭāhu dāran ḥasanatan wa-khadaman wa-ḥashaman
sentences.l: And-bestowed upon-him the-king, and-upon Bahādur, robes-of-honour splendid, and-gave-him a-house fine, and-servants and-retinue.
sentences.i: The king bestowed splendid robes of honour on him and on Bahādur, and gave him a fine house, with servants and a retinue.
sentences.n: The print has بهاذر, a misprint for بهادر, corrected here. khalaʿa ʿalā, 'to bestow (a robe) upon': the verb is properly 'to take off', the king's own robe given to the one honoured, and ʿalā marks him. khilaʿ, plural of khilʿa, 'robe of honour'; saniyya, 'splendid, of high worth', its shadda printed. khadam wa-ḥasham, 'servants and retinue', a rhyming pair.

sentences.t: وَأَنْعَمَ عَلَيْهِ بِجَمِيعِ مَا يَحْتَاجُ إِلَيْهِ وَرَتَّبَ لَهُ الرَّوَاتِبَ وَالْجِرَايَاتِ
sentences.tr: wa-anʿama ʿalayhi bi-jamīʿi mā yaḥtāju ilayhi wa-rattaba lahu al-rawātiba wa-al-jirāyāti
sentences.l: And-he-bestowed-favour upon-him with-all (of) what he-needs to-it, and-he-fixed for-him the-stipends and-the-allowances.
sentences.i: He granted him all he could need, and settled on him regular stipends and allowances.
sentences.n: anʿama ʿalā … bi-, 'to bestow on (someone) the gift of': ʿalā marks the one favoured and bi- the gift. iḥtāja ilā, 'to need': the verb takes ilā for the thing needed, here ilayhi, referring back to mā. rattaba lahu, 'he fixed for him': li- marks the one paid. rawātib, plural of rātib, a fixed salary; jirāyāt, plural of jirāya, a regular allowance of food or pay. The shadda of رتّب is printed.

sentences.t: وَأَمَرَهُ أَنْ يَبْحَثَ عَلَى أَخِيهِ الْأَسْعَدِ
sentences.tr: wa-amarahu an yabḥatha ʿalā akhīhi al-Asʿadi
sentences.l: And-he-ordered-him that he-search for his-brother al-Asʿad.
sentences.i: And he bade him search for his brother al-Asʿad.
sentences.n: The print has وامرة, a misprint for وامره, corrected here: wa-amarahu, 'and he ordered him'. baḥatha ʿalā, 'to search for', with ʿalā marking what is sought, where Classical has ʿan; a later usage, like fattasha ʿalā in the night before. The king is still the subject: he orders al-Amjad to search.

sentences.t: فَجَلَسَ الْأَمْجَدُ فِي مَرْتَبَةِ الْوَزِيرِ وَحَكَمَ وَعَدَلَ وَوَلَّى وَعَزَلَ وَأَخَذَ وَأَعْطَى
sentences.tr: fa-jalasa al-Amjadu fī martabati al-wazīri wa-ḥakama wa-ʿadala wa-wallā wa-ʿazala wa-akhadha wa-aʿṭā
sentences.l: And-sat al-Amjad in (the) rank (of) the-vizier, and-he-judged and-was-just, and-appointed and-dismissed, and-took and-gave.
sentences.i: So al-Amjad took his seat as vizier, and gave judgement and did justice, appointed and dismissed, took and gave.
sentences.n: The pairs are the stock description of a man in office: ḥakama wa-ʿadala, 'he ruled and was just'; wallā wa-ʿazala, 'he put men into office and turned them out'; akhadha wa-aʿṭā, 'he took and gave'. martaba, 'rank, place of dignity', also the cushioned seat that goes with it. The shadda of ولّى is printed.

sentences.t: وَأَرْسَلَ الْمُنَادِيَ فِي أَزِقَّةِ الْمَدِينَةِ يُنَادِي عَلَى أَخِيهِ الْأَسْعَدِ
sentences.tr: wa-arsala al-munādiya fī aziqqati al-madīnati yunādī ʿalā akhīhi al-Asʿadi
sentences.l: And-he-sent the-crier in (the) lanes (of) the-city, crying for his-brother al-Asʿad.
sentences.i: He sent the crier through the lanes of the city to cry for news of his brother al-Asʿad.
sentences.n: nādā ʿalā, 'to cry for', of a crier announcing something lost or sought: ʿalā marks it. The shadda of ازقّة is printed.

sentences.t: فَمَكَثَ مُدَّةَ أَيَّامٍ يُنَادِي فِى الشَّوَارِعِ وَالْأَسْوَاقِ فَمَا سَمِعَ لَهُ بِخَبَرٍ وَلَا وَقَعَ لَهُ عَلَى أَثَرٍ
sentences.tr: fa-makatha muddata ayyāmin yunādī fī al-shawāriʿi wa-al-aswāqi fa-mā samiʿa lahu bi-khabarin wa-lā waqaʿa lahu ʿalā atharin
sentences.l: And-he-remained a-space (of) days crying in the-streets and-the-markets, but-not he-heard for-him of-news and-not he-fell for-him upon a-trace.
sentences.i: For days on end he cried in the streets and the markets, but he heard no news of him and came upon no trace of him.
sentences.n: The subject is the crier, or al-Amjad through him. muddata ayyāmin, 'a space of days', accusative of time. samiʿa bi-, 'to hear of': bi- marks what is heard of; lahu, 'of him', li- marks the one the news concerns, as again in waqaʿa lahu ʿalā atharin, 'he fell upon a trace of him': waqaʿa ʿalā, 'to come upon'. khabar / athar is a rhyme. فى is printed with ى; kept as set.

sentences.t: هٰذَا مَاكَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِ الْأَمْجَدِ
sentences.tr: hādhā mā kāna min amri al-Amjadi
sentences.l: This (is) what was of (the) affair (of) al-Amjad.
sentences.i: So much for al-Amjad.
sentences.n: The same formula of transition as above; this time the print runs mā kāna together, ماكان; kept as set.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا مَاكَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِ الْأَسْعَدِ فَإِنَّ الْمَجُوسَ لَازَالُوا يُعَاقِبُونَهُ بِاللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهَارِ وَفِي الْعَشِيِّ وَالْإِبْكَارِ مُدَّةَ سَنَةٍ كَامِلَةٍ حَتَّى قَرُبَ عِيدُ الْمَجُوسِ
sentences.tr: wa-ammā mā kāna min amri al-Asʿadi fa-inna al-majūsa lā zālū yuʿāqibūnahu bi-al-layli wa-al-nahāri wa-fī al-ʿashiyyi wa-al-ibkāri muddata sanatin kāmilatin ḥattā qaruba ʿīdu al-majūsi
sentences.l: And-as-for what was of (the) affair (of) al-Asʿad, then-indeed the-Magians not-ceased punishing-him by-the-night and-the-day, and-in the-evening and-the-early-morning, (for) a-space (of) a-year complete, until drew-near (the) feast (of) the-Magians.
sentences.i: As for al-Asʿad, the Magians never left off tormenting him, by night and by day, at evening and at dawn, for a whole year, until the feast of the Magians drew near.
sentences.n: lā zālū with an imperfect, 'they did not cease to', so 'they kept on', with lā where Classical has mā zālū or lam yazālū; printed as one word, لازالوا, kept as set. bi-al-layli wa-al-nahāri, 'by night and by day': bi- of time. al-ʿashiyy wa-al-ibkār, 'the evening and the early morning', a Qurʾānic pair, and the rhyme of the phrase falls on al-nahār / al-ibkār; the shadda of العشيّ is printed. ʿāqaba, Form III, 'to punish'. The Magians are Bahrām and his people, who had taken al-Asʿad to be offered at their feast.

sentences.t: فَتَجَهَّزَ بَهْرَامُ الْمَجُوسِيُّ إِلَى السَّفَرِ وَهَيَّأَ لَهُ مَرْكَبًا
sentences.tr: fa-tajahhaza Bahrāmu al-Majūsiyyu ilā al-safari wa-hayyaʾa lahu markaban
sentences.l: And-equipped-himself Bahrām the-Magian for the-journey, and-made-ready for-himself a-ship.
sentences.i: Then Bahrām the Magian fitted himself out for the voyage and made a ship ready.
sentences.n: tajahhaza ilā, 'to get oneself ready for': ilā marks the end in view. hayyaʾa lahu, 'he made ready for himself (or for it)': li- marks the one it is readied for; the shadda and the hamza of هيّأ are printed, as is the shadda of تجهّز. Bahrām is a diptote, so nominative -u without tanwīn.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَ زَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka Shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And the-morning overtook Shahrazād, and-she-fell-silent from the-permitted speech.
sentences.i: And morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent from the speech allowed her.
sentences.n: The closing formula, as at the end of every night. The rhyme falls on al-ṣabāḥ / al-mubāḥ. The print sets the name as two words, شهر زاد; it is kept as set.
